body.content:
Current Good Manufacturing Practices, in plain language.

GMP is the FDA’s framework for supplement manufacturing. It covers every aspect of production: facility cleanliness, equipment calibration, batch record documentation, raw material verification, testing protocols, packaging integrity, and shipping conditions.

Being GMP compliant means we follow these practices. Being GMP certified by NSF and SQF means an independent third party audits our facility to verify we actually do. The difference matters: certification requires unannounced inspections, documentation review, and continuous evidence of compliance.

For private label brands, this means you can confidently tell your customers that every product you sell was manufactured under the same standards as the brands they already trust.

accordion.accordion_title: How much do private label supplements actually cost?
accordion.content: Per-bottle cost depends on the formulation complexity, ingredient cost, and order volume. Most private label SKUs land between $4 and $15 per bottle at standard volumes. Larger volumes drive per-unit cost down. We provide transparent pricing during our consultation.

accordion.accordion_title: What are your minimum order quantities?
accordion.content: Our minimums are intentionally low to let new brands launch without massive upfront inventory commitment. Typical MOQs are in the low hundreds of units per SKU. Larger volumes get better per-unit pricing.

accordion.accordion_title: How long from first conversation to first product shipping?
accordion.content: Most clients launch within 8 to 12 weeks of first conversation. Once labels are approved, production takes 3 to 4 weeks. The variable is how quickly you finalize product selection and approve label design.

accordion.accordion_title: Do you handle FDA labeling and compliance?
accordion.content: We provide FDA-compliant label templates and review your custom labels for compliance with structure-function claims, supplement facts panel requirements, and required disclaimers. Your brand is ultimately responsible for compliance, but we make it dramatically easier.

accordion.accordion_title: What is the difference between private label and custom formulation?
accordion.content: Private label means putting your brand on our existing formulations. Fast (3 to 4 weeks after label approval), low minimums, immediate market entry. Custom formulation means developing a new product to your specifications. Slower (6 to 12 months), higher minimums, but proprietary ownership.

body.chapter_title: The basics of private label supplements

body.content:
What are private label supplements?

Private labeling is putting your brand on existing, high-quality nutritional supplement formulas with legal permission from their provider.

It allows healthcare practitioners and entrepreneurs to build a niche brand and grow their business with less liability risk because they may be partially protected by the supplier's compliance and insurance umbrella policy.

Private labeling is an attractive option because research and development, legal considerations, marketing material, and FDA approved labels are provided by the supplement provider, enabling practitioners and business owners to reap the benefits without the time and expense of creating a new formula from scratch.

What is the difference between private label and white label supplements?

The terms “private label” and “white label” are often used interchangeably. In the context of marketing supplements, there isn't much difference between them, except a private label specifies the ingredients and concentration of nutrients included in the product. A white label, on the other hand, often means simply placing a brand logo on an otherwise generic product package.
